Consult Summary:
- Acute onset left arm weakness with focal neurologic symptoms (dysphagia, speech difficulty, left facial tingling) upon waking; concern for stroke; ambulance arranged to transport patient to local hospital for stroke assessment and potential treatment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: woke about 1 hour ago with inability to move left arm; currently left arm remains immobile but not painful.
- Associated symptoms: tingling on the left side of the face; difficulty swallowing; speech is becoming harder/slower.
- Onset/duration/progression: symptoms began about 1 hour ago and persist; no reported improvement.
- Exposures/initiating factors: woke without known awkward sleep position or new bed; no chest pain, no loss of consciousness reported.
- Negative/positive symptoms: no left leg symptoms; no discoloration or coldness in the arm; no facial asymmetry reported by patient.
- Additional context: patient lives alone; no one else at home; ambulance being arranged; currently on a telephone appointment.
- Review of systems: not extensively documented beyond the neurologic symptoms above.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.
- No other illnesses documented.

Medications:
- Metformin.
- Losartan.
- Amlodipine.
- Allergies: penicillin.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Former smoker.
- Alcohol: drinks beer; typical weekend consumption and some during the week.

Family History:
- Father with heart disease.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Exam findings: left arm immobile; dysphagia; speech becoming harder/slower; tingling on left face. No other exam findings documented. (Remote/telephone assessment; no formal in-person neuro exam available.)

Investigations:
- None completed at time of contact; ambulance to perform hospital-based stroke workup.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute cerebrovascular event (stroke) presenting with left arm weakness, dysphagia, and speech difficulties.
  - Plan:
    - Activate emergency transport to local hospital A&E for urgent stroke evaluation and possible treatment.
    - EMS will assess and notify stroke team; a treatment option may be considered depending on evaluation.
    - Patient instructed to keep front door accessible for EMS (sit in hallway) and remains on line until EMS arrival.
    - No at-home treatment beyond awaiting EMS; monitor symptoms and await further instructions from EMS/hospital.

  - Vital signs (none documented).
  - Detailed neurological exam results (no formal exam findings documented beyond patient-reported symptoms).
  - Specific onset time (provided as “about 1 hour ago,” acceptable but could be exact if known).
  - Medications: dosing, routes, and frequencies not documented.
  - Imaging/lab results (not yet available; none provided).
  - Functional assessment or baseline status (not documented).
- Internal conflicts:
  - None identified; transcripts align with concern for stroke and actions taken.
- Transcript quality:
  - Telephone encounter with some pauses and incomplete details; generally clear regarding symptom onset and emergent plan. Some gaps in objective data due to remote assessment.
